text_block_list.name: Aston Machan
text_block_list.text:
All hot pots eaten by sumo wrestlers are 
called 'chanko nabe.' So wouldn't it make 
sense to call any hot pot made by Machan 
'Ma-chanko nabe'?

text_block_list.name: Hishi Akebono
text_block_list.text:
"Ma-chan Chanko Stew"! Sounds wonderful~! 
What kind of stew is it? Tell me, tell 
me~!

text_block_list.name: Aston Machan
text_block_list.text:
First, upon the battlefield of an iron 
pot, we bring the fruit to total 
reconciliation with lemon juice and cane 
sugar, simmering it until it turns a foxy 
brown.

text_block_list.name: Aston Machan
text_block_list.text:
In the meantime, gently pinch and mix 
together the flour, sugar, and chilled 
butter—just like giving a massage to 
Grandpa's shoulders.

text_block_list.name: Hishi Akebono
text_block_list.text:
It kind of feels like a crumble, doesn't 
it?

text_block_list.name: Aston Machan
text_block_list.text:
And then, while the pot is completely off 
its guard, we mix them together, sending 
them on a vacation in the oven to get nice 
and sun-tanned.

text_block_list.name: Aston Machan
text_block_list.text:
“—And so, the 'Ma-chanko Hot Pot' is 
complete. It pairs well with custard and 
ice cream alike— quite the clever little 
dish.”

text_block_list.name: Hishi Akebono
text_block_list.text:
It looks delicious, like apple crumble~! 
Oh right, you can totally make it in a 
pot, so that counts as a hot pot dish too, 
doesn't it?♪

text_block_list.name: Aston Machan
text_block_list.text:
Wonder if it'd catch on, wonder if it'd 
sell. 'Ma-chan Chanko Hotpot'.
